PullRequest.Title: quickinput: Distinguish appearance selection from focus
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #344283
Fixes #344285
Related: #344641

Icon and color pickers should distinguish the current selection from the control receiving keyboard input. This keeps the selected item readable without making it look like a second focused input.

The icon picker's keyboard behavior was already correct: Search initially owns focus while the first icon is selected. The problem was that the selected icon reused the focus colors. This change uses neutral selection colors while preserving the actual keyboard-focus outline and existing Search/Tab/arrow behavior.

- Apply the same treatment to color choices and **Reset to default** in the shared pickers used by terminal tabs and session groups. Ordinary Quick Picks retain their existing selection colors.
- Label the noninteractive footer **Icon name: add**, so it reads as the current selection's caption rather than an action.
- Give the divider its own bounds above Reset. Previously, its border made the inner entry taller than the selectable row, pushing the label down. The entry now fills its row with centered content; no text offset is used. Decorative dividers stay out of option counts and keyboard-focus targets.
- Let the title bar inherit the picker frame's corner radius so high-contrast top corners remain continuous.

### How to test

1. In the Agents window, right-click a session group and choose **Change Icon** or **Change Color**. Search, Tab into the icons, use arrows, and Tab to Reset. Selection should use a neutral fill; the focused control should retain its independent outline. The icon footer remains a caption.
2. Focus **Reset to default** in each picker. Its label should be vertically centered and its divider should sit outside the outlined row. Escape should cancel without changing the existing icon/color.
3. Use a terminal tab's **Change Icon** and **Change Color** actions to exercise the same shared controls. Check the picker corners in the high-contrast themes.

### Validation

- Targeted icon, base ObjectTree, Quick Input, shared picker, session appearance and terminal tests: **86 passed**. Regression cases cover visible section navigation, divider-excluding accessibility positions, widget-toggle state, action-bearing headers and filtering boundaries.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` and `npm run typecheck-client` — passed on the final candidate.
- Targeted TypeScript ESLint, stylesheet lint and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Native Code OSS before/after validation in Dark 2026 and High Contrast Light. Existing keyboard behavior and the high-contrast corner fix were also manually confirmed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call chain, cache reset, full-sibling iteration, and prior O(1) behavior are explicit in the repository. Exact milliseconds vary with provider size, but the added O(n) CPU/allocation on a virtualized picker’s render-critical path is deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work plus one Map entry and position object for every sibling item
Findings.PerformanceScaling: After each items assignment, the cache is cleared; rendering the first row then performs two full sibling filters and populates the map for all n siblings, so cold open/update cost and allocation grow O(n) even though the list virtualizes DOM rows.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased picker-open/update latency and CPU/GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, AbstractTree computed aria-setsize from parentNode.visibleChildrenCount and aria-posinset from node.visibleChildIndex, both O(1) for each rendered row, and Quick Input retained no parallel position map.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new QuickInputAccessibilityProvider handles those attributes itself; on the first rendered element in each sibling group it copies/filters the full sibling collection twice and inserts every sibling into positions. The companion AbstractTree change now delegates to these methods.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 316-324 introduce the full sibling scans and per-sibling Map population, while the added AbstractTree delegation at lines 184-196 makes this provider execute instead of the previous constant-time tree metadata path.
Findings.Title: Avoid indexing the entire Quick Pick on first render
Findings.Impact: Opening or refreshing a large flat Quick Pick—such as an extension-provided picker or the command palette’s full command set—now synchronously walks and allocates for every item before the first virtualized rows finish rendering. Reassigning items repeats the cost, which can visibly delay large picker updates and add GC pressure.
Findings.Evidence: QuickPick.items synchronously calls QuickInputList.setElements during update; _setElementsToTree clears positions, and ListView.updateItemInDOM immediately requests getSetSize/getPosInSet for rendered rows. This added cold path calls getSiblings(element).filter(...), filters that result again, then creates a Map value for every sibling. Built-in command quick access groups all registered editor/global commands, while the shared Quick Pick API permits uncapped extension item arrays; the work is therefore collection-sized rather than viewport-sized.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the existing O(1) tree size/index path when a parent has no decorative divider. For parents that do, compute divider-adjusted counts/offsets during the existing tree-build pass (or cache compact per-parent divider metadata) rather than materializing a position object for every item during row rendering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, filter, or refresh a large Quick Pick such as the command palette, file quick access, or an extension-provided picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider results are assigned to QuickPick.items, which synchronously rebuilds the QuickInputList and renders the first virtualized rows before the picker/update is usable. The new accessibility position scan runs in that render-critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Workspace file search for global file quick-access results
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pre-existing search request per settled filter, capped to 512 results by AnythingQuickAccessProvider.MAX_RESULTS
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same file search occurred before the diff; returned items used O(1) tree metadata for ARIA position/size rather than a collection-wide position map.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Global file results await the search, after which applying the returned items incurs the new synchronous indexing cost; local/fast picks can appear earlier.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: AI related-command lookup when natural-language command search is enabled
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one pre-existing debounced request per active command filter, with up to five related picks consumed
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The lookup and second items application were pre-existing; the latter did not eagerly index every sibling for accessibility attributes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local command picks can be shown first; the remote result is off the initial local-pick critical path but applying additional picks triggers another list rebuild.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective visible sibling count after provider filtering/grouping: built-in file quick access caps global file results at 512, the command palette includes all enabled registered commands grouped by separators, and extension-provided Quick Pick arrays are not capped by this widget.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The changed tree rebuild, accessibility attribute calculation, sibling scans, and Map population are synchronous on the UI thread. Provider fast/slow results may arrive asynchronously, but every applied items array independently resets and rebuilds this cache.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold after every items assignment and when custom-widget state changes because positions is cleared. The first rendered child of each parent scans and caches all siblings; later rows under that parent are warm until the next reset. There is no negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: items assignment, cache reset, first-row ARIA calculation, full sibling scans, and per-sibling Map insertion are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact delay depends on provider size and engine allocation cost, but the widget accepts uncapped arrays and the added O(n) scan/allocation is deterministic on each cold list build.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the PR replaces constant-time tree metadata with eager collection-wide work for every Quick Pick, although decorative dividers are used only by a narrow picker shape.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open terminal/session-group color pickers or the shared profile/terminal icon picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construct a small in-memory item list or icon grid, assign it to Quick Input, build local DOM rows, and show the picker. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is reached by the changed appearance code.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed terminal color palette and a bounded built-in icon catalog; the Reset divider adds one local tree element.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All changed work is synchronous UI/DOM work; there is no parallel boundary work or queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A new picker starts cold and is disposed on close. The accessibility map is rebuilt when items/widget state is assigned, but these appearance lists are small and have no cross-picker cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed callers only set flags/items/widgets and local styles.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Small fixed cardinality makes the added local divider/layout work negligible in these intended appearance flows.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for the appearance pickers; their bounded list sizes do not create a concrete regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Navigate between Quick Pick sections with the next/previous-section keyboard commands
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A keybinding synchronously calls QuickInputList.focus, traverses the visible tree to collect section starts, updates focus, and reveals the target row before input handling returns.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: All visible tree elements after filtering; command palette sections can contain all enabled registered commands.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI-thread key event with no coalescing or background work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No navigation cache is used; each section-navigation command reconstructs the sections array. Filtering reduces effective cardinality before traversal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the traversal mechanism, lower for meaningful impact at realistic cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The new traversal is O(n), but built-in lists are generally bounded to hundreds or low thousands and section-navigation is an explicit, infrequent command; no concrete user-visible delay is established independently of the reported cold-render issue.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the full traversal is less efficient than directional early-stop navigation, but evidence does not establish a meaningful performance regression for this infrequent command.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 16 changed files. Reported one render-critical eager indexing regression in the shared Quick Pick accessibility path; appearance styling/divider work and section navigation did not meet the threshold for additional findings.
